text: Code quality (explicit error paths), advisory only — `seedValue` in packages/tinyapp-history/src/mutant.ts is `JSON.parse(text(row.from_value))`, and `text()` maps a null column to the empty string. A `modified`/`removed` row that arrives with a null `from_value` therefore fails as an opaque `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` from deep inside a map, rather than as a statement about the row

the same null-to-`''` fallback in `tableOf`/`editOf` would silently emit an edit naming the empty table/row/cell. Well-formed `dolt_diff_cells` rows never hit either path (M1's contract guarantees the `from_` side on `modified`/`removed` and the `to_` side on `added`), so this is not a missing requirement — no leg of the Proof names it, legs (b)–(h) all pass on the shapes the task specifies, and EXAM EVIDENCE is exit 0. Worth a throwing guard naming the row (`throw new Error(\`diff row ${diff_type} ${table}/${row}/${cell} carries no from_value\`)`) if this module later reads rows that a sibling did not build.

Redundant double cast masks a future regex change. `packages/tinyapp-history/src/transitions.ts:85` writes `const [, name, inner] = match as unknown as [string, string, string];`. Under the Run line's flags (and the package tsconfig copied from `packages/tinyapp-exam/tsconfig.json`, which sets `strict` but not `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), destructuring a `RegExpExecArray` already yields `string` for both captures, so the assertion buys nothing — and because it goes through `unknown`, it would keep compiling if `CALL` ever lost its second capture group, handing `inner` an `undefined` that `JSON.parse('[' + inner + ']')` would turn into a silently-wrong parse of `[undefined]` rather than a type error. Everything the task requires is present and evidenced: Produces `parseMessage` (transitions.ts:82), `listTransitions` (:105), `renderTransitions` (:132) and `Transition` (:52) with `HistoryReader`, `LogEntry` and `DiffRow` spelled locally and no sibling import, matching the Context

legs (b)–(d) at session-transitions.test.ts:319/328/337, (e) at :349 with a full `toEqual` on the transition including `changes`, (f) at :367 asserting both seeds, the second expected and `reader.asked` as exactly `('c1','c2')` then `('c2','c3')`, (g) at :387 covering the one-line render, the two-line join, the `(2 changes)` plural and 8-character slicing, (h) at :426 spawning the Proof's `Run:` line, and leg (a)'s single column-0 `stateExam` at :445 in the shape the Context spells, running the listed call by name through `client/src/storeData`'s own `setTodoCompleted`. `state-exams/seeds/two-open-todos.json` and `state-exams/expected/two-todos-first-done.json` are present at BASE with the contents the Context quotes, so no sibling-owned dependency is missing. The diff touches only the two declared FILES, deletes nothing, adds no debug code and no unrelated refactor
no commit hash is pinned (the stubs are the `c0`–`c3` literals M2/M3 name)

the exam calls `stateExam(` exactly once at column 0 and nothing else from `tinyapp-exam` at top level, and imports the module by relative path. RUN, EXAM and CHECK evidence all exit 0 (`lint:state` 0 findings, `client/src` byte-identical to BASE) and the state-exam record shows the `todos/0/completed` mutant killed. undeclared amendment: Proof leg (g) spells `bun run history promote <tmpfile> 3 derived-complete-first-todo` "spawned with `cwd` a second, empty temp directory". `tests/state-exams/derived-exam.test.ts` instead spawns `bun <ROOT>/packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts promote …` with that cwd (patch lines 916-948). The substitution is well-founded — the file's own header records that `bun run <script>` resolves the script by walking up from the spawn cwd, so from an empty temp directory it never reaches the CLI at all — and everything else the leg asks (exit 0, stdout exactly the three relative paths in order, the recursive listing exactly those three paths, each file `toBe` the committed one) stays live. But the divergence is declared only in a code comment inside the exam file

the AMENDMENTS block carries one entry, and it is about `cli.ts`'s `here()` helper, not about re-aiming leg (g). Rule 9 grades a divergence the diff shows and no entry declares as minor, naming the clause: Proof leg (g).

The `npm_config_local_prefix` branch of `here()` (packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts:69-74) — the whole substance of the declared AMENDMENTS entry — is exercised by no leg. Leg (g) spawns `bun <abs path>/cli.ts` with cwd the temp directory, so `resolve(process.cwd()) === CLI_ROOT` is false and the env-var branch never runs

legs (c), (d) and (i) never write a promotion. Replacing `here()` with a bare `process.cwd()` leaves every test in the file green, so the branch is untested code under duty 5, and M3's "`bun run history promote <file> 3 <slug>` writes exactly three files under the current directory" is settled only for the `bun <file>` spawn shape, never for the `bun run history` shape the clause names. The entry's `why` is also in tension with the exam's own measurement: the scenario it guards against (`bun run history promote` spawned with cwd a foreign directory) is the one the file's header records as unreachable, since bun cannot resolve the script from there. Either add a leg that pins the env-var branch (spawn `bun run history promote` from a directory inside the tree and assert where the three files land) or drop the branch back to `process.cwd()` as the Context spells it.

`list` and `promote` open their argument with `openHistory(file)` (packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts:132), and per M1 of task 1 `openHistory` creates the DoltLite file when it is absent. So `bun run history list /no/such/session.dolt` creates an empty history at that path, prints `renderTransitions([])` — a single blank line — and exits 0, and `promote` against the same path fails only later, on the out-of-range index. The Context's error sentence is "a missing verb, file, out-of-range `n` or a `promote` that throws prints the message to stderr and exits non-zero"

only the missing *argument* reading is implemented. No leg covers it either way. Guarding the two read verbs with an existence check — `if (!existsSync(file)) fail(`history ${verb}: no history file at ${file}`)` before the open — closes the gap without touching `record`, which is the one verb that should create.

concern: plan-defect: Proof leg (g) spawns `bun run history promote <tmpfile> 3 <slug>` with `cwd` "a second, empty temp directory". If that directory is created under `os.tmpdir()`, the command exits 1 with `error: Script not found "history"` — `bun run` walks up from cwd for a package.json and finds none — which no implementation of the CLI can affect. The leg passes for a temp directory created inside the repository root (as `views.test.ts` itself does with `mkdtempSync(join(ROOT, 'state-exams', 'lint-tmp-'))`), and for a direct `bun packages/tinyapp-history/src/cli.ts …` spawn from any directory
both were measured green against the committed files. Disclosed so the exam's author picks one of those two spellings rather than `os.tmpdir()` + `bun run`.
